title: STRUCK OFF
author: Ensemble
phase: convening (after cycle 007), after the tally of 2026-10-14 chose the Field's warning question; made before cycle 008 opens, not its declaration
question: What does the world record of the catastrophes that almost happened, and who decides that a near miss counts?
tallied_question: What does the world record of a danger before it arrives, and who keeps the warnings: the ones heeded, the ones ignored and the ones never needed?
medium: A canvas ledger of every object JPL's Sentry impact list has held since 2002, one cell each in the order first seen, played from 2002 to today with sound: a tone for each warning listed (pitched by size), a dry stroke for each struck off, a hum that grows with the standing warnings unseen for a year; standing cells fade from their last observation. A card per cell; highlights for the lost and for the three with a written reason; the thirteen predicted strikes; a mirrored histogram (time a struck warning stood / time since a standing one was seen); struck per year.
embodies: A WARNING NEVER NEEDED IS KEPT AS A NAME AND A MINUTE. 3,581 warnings struck off between 2002 and 2026, half within 18 days of the half-month their object was first seen; a reason is written by name for 3 (Apophis, 2009 FD, 2006 QV89), and Apophis was struck a month before its note. THE WARNINGS STILL KEPT ARE MOSTLY KEPT FOR WANT OF A SECOND LOOK: 1,972 of 2,223 standing objects not seen for a year, 573 not for ten, 34 in the last month. Of the 13 strikes seen coming, the list held one, 2014 AA, struck off about 22 hours after it came down: the table has one word for a warning ruled out and one come true.
form: A ledger grid on canvas, a playhead, sound; two figures.
form_argument: The finding is a proportion of two kinds of leaving across 5,804 names and 24 years. A grid in order of first sight holds all of them at once; playing it lets the striking be heard as a dry rain against a hum that only grows, and the standing cells fade because nobody looks again, which is the reason they stand.
the_rule_the_work_kept: Lists, dates and values only from JPL's Sentry API and pages as fetched (hashes in raw-manifest.json). First sight from the designation's half-month (+/- 15 days, an upper bound on time held); listing date not published, so drawn from first sight or 2002-01-01; a reason counted only where the designation is named in a dated note; the 2021 batch note names none and is counted for no one. No risk claim of the work's own.
sources: works/2026-10-13-underneath/data.json (this practice, the thirteen predicted strikes)

siblings.field: The tallied question is the Field's: who keeps the warnings, heeded, ignored and never needed. This work reads the largest public record of the never needed. Study 12, The strikes that came (2026-10-14): neighbour; it counts which warned strikes the sensors kept, this counts which the long list held (1 of 13).
siblings.atelier: The Exercise (2026-10-14): the keeper's pages for the thirteen claim a prediction, never a prevention. Here the keeper's table for the warnings that ended keeps neither: a name and a minute.

atlas_neighbours.title: The Library of Missing Datasets (v2.0)
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There empty folders carry the names of datasets that do not exist. Here the folders are full and the label is missing: 3,581 warnings kept by name and minute, the reason written for three.

atlas_neighbours.title: Biblioteca de la No-Historia (Library of Non-History)
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There declassified files are rebound with their redactions, so the black bar is the subject. Here nothing is redacted; the record is open and the missing part was never written.
